question: Effect of active tDCS against sham on global cognition in pooled MCI and AD populations, from meta-analyses of RCTs. The question, comparison and channel (cognitive test scores) are the same. The pooled trial sets differ: P-832's tDCS subgroup has 6 studies, while P-705's MMSE analysis has 10 RCTs in 9 studies with 451 participants.
metric: Mismatch: P-832's tDCS estimate is an SMD pooled over MMSE, MoCA or ADAS-Cog; P-705's is a mean difference in MMSE points. Neither paper reports the other's metric for tDCS.

figures.P-832: tDCS subgroup, global cognition: SMD 1.20 (95% CI -0.26 to 2.65), p = 0.107, I2 = 93.6%. Not significant; the point estimate favours tDCS.
figures.P-705: MMSE: MD 1.96 (95% CI 0.95 to 2.97), p = 0.0001, I2 = 92%. The sensitivity analysis gives 1.76 (1.29 to 2.23); MoCA MD 1.51 (0.17 to 2.85). Significant; favours tDCS. A rough scale check, not a printed figure: with an MMSE SD of 3-4 points, P-705's interval corresponds to an SMD of about 0.24-0.99 (0.95/4 to 2.97/3), which lies inside P-832's interval. The intervals overlap for any plausible SD.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-832's MMSE-only subgroup (SMD 0.32, -0.20 to 0.85) pools rTMS and tDCS, so it is not a tDCS figure. P-705 reports no SMD.
reason: The two estimates use different metrics (an SMD over mixed instruments against an MMSE mean difference; condition 2), and both favour tDCS. P-832's is non-significant with an interval from -0.26 to 2.65; P-705's is significant. A significant estimate against a non-significant one qualifies only if the intervals exclude each other, and here they overlap on any plausible conversion (condition 4). P-832's authors attribute their null to low power. The record's 'opposite conclusions about whether tDCS works ... significance and direction' misreads the pair, since the directions agree (condition 6).
